svg.aria-label: Two separately allocated scatterlist arrays joined by sg_chain into one logical byte stream. The last entry of the first array is not a data descriptor: its page_link holds a pointer to the second array with the SG_CHAIN bit set, and its offset and length are zero. The final entry of the second array carries the SG_END bit, at which the walk stops. A descriptor records a page, an offset and a length, but nothing about where the page came from or who owns it.
svg.title: Chaining of scatterlists
svg.desc: Two bands, each holding an array of scatterlist descriptors drawn as boxes with their page_link, offset and length fields. The upper band is array A, allocated by the caller; its third entry is a chain entry whose page_link points at array B with the SG_CHAIN flag set and whose offset and length are cleared to zero. An arrow leads from that entry down into the lower band, array B, a separate allocation whose final entry carries the SG_END flag. A note beneath the two bands records that a descriptor names a page, an offset and a length but nothing about the page's provenance, so a page-cache page spliced in from a read-only file is indistinguishable from a kernel scratch buffer once the two are chained together.

g.text: ONE LOGICAL BYTE STREAM, TWO SEPARATELY ALLOCATED ARRAYS
the chain entry holds no data
Its low bit marks page_link as a pointer to the next array rather than to a
page; sg_chain() clears offset and length because they are meaningless here.
ARRAY B — struct scatterlist sgl_B[2], A SEPARATE ALLOCATION
A walk with sg_next() crosses the boundary without noticing it: one stream, A[0] | A[1] | B[0] | B[1].
WHAT THE DESCRIPTOR DOES NOT RECORD
A descriptor names a page, an offset and a length — not where the page came from, who owns
it, or whether it was obtained for reading only. Once chained, a page-cache page spliced in from
a read-only file is indistinguishable from a buffer the kernel allocated for scratch.
